analyst_summary: Churchill Resources (CRI.V) holds the Hells Gate district in Central Newfoundland — a western-hemisphere antimony and polymetallic project that continues to broaden in geological scope. No new disclosures surfaced in the July 5, 2026 scan; all web fetch attempts returned 403 from datacenter IPs. The most recent material development remains the high-grade zinc grab samples released July 4, 2026 from Black Raven — three samples returning 5.25%, 11.03%, and 12.11% Zn alongside high-grade gold, silver, and lead — adding zinc to a commodity assemblage that already includes antimony, gold, silver, and molybdenum. China's 2024 antimony export controls remain in force, providing durable macro tailwind. Structural constraints are unchanged: at 316.7M shares outstanding with no NI 43-101 resource estimate, per-share upside is unquantifiable and scoring is capped. Confidence remains LOW — no resource, no accessible IR page, no insider ownership data. Key inflection points: (1) drill-hole assay results from the evaluation program confirming the Black Raven and Pomley Cove Pond systems extend at depth and economic widths, (2) maiden inferred resource under NI 43-101, (3) strategic partnership or institutional placement validating NAV.
